note: Files: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base, cue; 500 rows, 27 cap_hit true) and runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL, plain; 500 rows, 6 cap_hit true), the paths the recipe names; if absent the script fetches them from S3 (inventory.md commands) into runs/theory-tests/. Kept: cap_hit is False and non-empty text; one row per problem_index (sample is 0 everywhere). Exposure and events are pooled over all kept rows of each model (unpaired), as the recipe says 'summed over all kept rows of a model'. alt_measured: same statistic on the problems where both models have a kept row (paired reading). Brace balancing counts every '{' and '}' literally, including escaped \{ \}; a box result position equal to len(text) adds no exposure. Duplicate result positions are merged. The stored texts start with the tail of the prompt (e.g. ' line!' or ' tag.'); the text field is used as is, without stripping it. d(i) before the first result is i, so the opening of every answer counts in B1/B2 before any result has been stated, which mixes 'right after a result' with 'start of the answer'. Bootstrap over problems (union of problem indices) with pooled ratios recomputed per resample; an undefined resample is sorted as -inf. n = number of problems with at least one kept row.

Same files, filters, result positions, d(i), events and exposure as k=1. Statistic R_1 = (1000*events_B1/exposure_B1 for T2) / (same for T1), pooled over all kept rows of each model. Undefined (refuted_without_number) only if the T1 B1 rate is 0 (or a B1 exposure is 0); a T2 B1 rate of 0 gives R_1 = 0, which is defined and refuted (< 0.75). alt_measured: paired reading (problems where both models have a kept row). B1 includes the first 200 characters of every answer (d = i before any result), not only positions right after a stated result; this could raise or lower R_1 relative to the theory's intended 'right after a result' reading. Undefined bootstrap resamples (practically impossible) are sorted as +inf.

Same as k=1 but exposure counts only indices i < len(text)/2 (integer i < ceil(L/2), L = length of the comma-deleted text) and only events whose start index is < len(text)/2; d(i) and result positions are computed on the full comma-deleted text (results in the second half cannot affect first-half indices anyway). Undefined (refuted_without_number) if a T1 rate in B1 or B4 is 0, T2 exposure in B4 is 0, or the T2 B1 rate is 0 (R_1 = 0 makes R_4/R_1 undefined). alt_measured: paired reading (problems where both models have a kept row). B4 exposure in the first half needs answers with 1500+ result-free characters early on, so B4 may be thin and the ratio noisy; B1 again includes each answer's opening 200 characters.
